ratings.comment: Professor Martin is one of the kindest and most caring professors in the Art History department. She's eager to learn what students are interested in and lets you explore almost anything for projects. Lectures were interesting with several guest speakers making appearances, which may be a con for some, but I always liked learning from them.
Ann is so kind and cares about her students! The coursework is very interesting, and the more you put into the class the more you will get out of it.

If you took her class expecting it to be an easy grade, that's simply your fault... you actually need a passion (and appreciation) for the subject matter. Deeply engaging instruction, some of the best discussions I've experienced in class, and very FAIR grading. 10/10 would take again.

Professor Martin wants her students to succeed. She has a lot of experience and uses it to her students advantage which also makes her lecture topics interesting. She has a ton of knowledge in her field and if you want to take a Material Culture class you should to take it with her. She's very welcoming so go to her office hours!

Lectures are very irrelevant as they relate nothing to the assignments. There are few assignments and grades in the grade book, but when something is assigned, the rubric is vague and makes no sense. Professor is very unorganized and can't even explain her own assignments. The class isn't interesting at all. AVOID IT

This class is hell. Had to pregame just to get through it. Ann only lectured like three times, otherwise brought in guest lecturers who had nothing to do with the material that was read. Assigned two lengthy readings per class period, which were never discussed. Expected us to go to events outside of class. There was a group project.

Clearly passionate about the topic, and that's part of the charm. However, the class is extremely unorganized. Expectations are not vague and not clearly stated. This in turn hurts your grade when they mark down points for missing an element in your paper that was never expected of your in the first place.

Ann was nice and cared about feedback from students but the class its self was ill prepared and I didn't feel like I learned anything valuable. All graded assignments were about reading a complex textbook and the theories weren't discussed in class ever. Mediocre material culture studies class as best. Very chaotic and poorly taught in a useful way

Prof. Martin is a really nice person & loves to get to know her students.  That being said she is disorganized and this definitely effects the class structure.  Some assignments were harshly graded and others were not.  I love the professor but the class was really unpredictable.

She assigned a 3 page paper on the last day of class. It wasn't on the syllabus and she gave us only 4 days to complete it even though we were all in the middle of exams. She's very nice but not very organized or considerate.

Nice person but she's unbelievably disorganized and as a result is an outrageously ineffective teacher at the 400+ level. Had a tendency to assign large research projects (even our FINAL PROJECT) with little to no warning. She never shows up on time and her lack of preparation is constantly evident. There is no excuse for this kind of laziness.

Professor Martin is really great and sweet! She is a little disorganized but you can tell she really wants everyone to succeed. If you go to lectures, takes good notes and read the textbook you will get an A. Plus, if you participate she definitely is not opposed to boosting up your grade. The class was super interesting and I would recommend it!!

Martin is really nice.  She love what she teaches which is great, but she isn't very organized.  I lectures are way more important than the readings.  Easy class if you pay attention and study.  Usually I need to make flash cards to study for art history exams, but I didn't need to for this class.

Prof. Martin is one of the most sweet ladies teaching at the UW. She is very positive, straightforward,& helpful to her students. She is VERY interested in art history. She is one of those teachers who is a bit naive, but that is part of her sweet nature. Doesn't know how to work technology if her life depended on it. I would recommend her highly!
